clue.text: Policeman arrests me, a killer about to take a fall

indicators.note: the policeman arrests, so holds within him, the words that follow

parts.note: copper is everyday slang for a police officer
taken as written

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the killer round so it reads the other way

parts.note: an orc is a killer whale, an orca

explanation.surface: A police officer nabs a murderer and the narrator, who is about to tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killer' is the killer whale; 'about' turns it round and 'arrests' places the result, with ME A, in the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to come a cropper is to fall heavily, or by extension to fail badly.

clue.text: Cannot even box

parts.note: can't is the contracted form of cannot
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot box evenly, perhaps a clumsy fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces drop their apostrophes: CAN'T and E'EN. 'box' is a noun, a canteen of cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a case or chest holding a set of cutlery, a kind of storage container.

clue.text: Gateman could become an influential person

indicators.note: the gateman's letters could become another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: A humble doorkeeper might rise to become someone important.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy, powerful figure in business or industry.

clue.text: Live broadcast set up after a race by a man

indicators.note: after places the broadcast piece behind the race and the man

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the broadcast word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: to emit is to broadcast or send out

explanation.surface: A live outside broadcast is staged after a race involving one man.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'set up' reads upwards; 'after' places the broadcast word last. 'Live' means happening then, not recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done live happens in real time, simultaneously rather than recorded for later.

clue.text: Engaged in competition, server finally beat receiver

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word server

parts.note: in tennis a server who aces the receiver beats them with an unreturnable serve

explanation.surface: A tennis match in which the server ends up beating the receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to compete for speed against rivals, so the past tense means took part in a contest.

clue.text: Paddy dresses as an agricultural labourer

indicators.note: the paddy dresses, or wraps around, the two little words that follow

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, also called a pet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Paddy turns out to be dressed as a farm worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a man's name or a rice field, but it is a tantrum, PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a small farmer or farm worker of low social rank.

clue.text: What determines the nature of city church?

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in western Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A question asking what gives a cathedral city its true character.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of a thing is its intrinsic quality, the core that makes it what it is.

clue.text: Secret procedure points the way to outshine other performers

parts.note: stealth is a furtive, secret way of proceeding
E is the compass point east
S is the compass point south
how means the way or manner

explanation.surface: A covert method is said to show the route to upstaging fellow actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' gives two compass letters, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to steal the show is to attract the most praise and attention in a performance.

clue.text: Child will come round by this evening

indicators.note: the child will come round, so encircle, the word for near

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh means near, close by

explanation.surface: A youngster will visit at some point this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means near here, NIGH, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the coming night or evening of the present day.

clue.text: Great book — girl and I are absorbed in small volume

indicators.note: the girl and I are absorbed in, so sit inside, the small volume

parts.note: cc is the cubic centimetre, a small unit of volume
a lass is a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl and the narrator lose themselves in a slim edition of a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost the 'I'; the page prints it. 'volume' looks like a book, but it is cubic capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of literature of lasting, acknowledged excellence.

clue.text: In UN, Dutch start off lively debate

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad or astray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: At the United Nations, the Dutch delegate kicks off a spirited argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' looks like a phrase meaning begin; 'off' is the anagram signal working on UN, DUTCH and START, and 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from swordplay: the cut and thrust of argument is its vigorous exchange of points.

clue.text: In the mean time girl stays in

indicators.note: the girl stays in, so sits inside, the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, a young woman remains at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the mean time' reads as meanwhile; 'mean' alone is the definition, the arithmetic mean.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is their arithmetic average.

clue.text: Granted dispensation for police operation

indicators.note: a dispensation hands out or redistributes, so the letters are dealt out afresh

explanation.surface: Permission is given for the police to carry out a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a systematic sweep by police to catch wanted suspects.

clue.text: Suffering from strain in the past, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about something that happened earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed and nervous describes someone strained; in grammar the past is one example of a verb's time form.

clue.text: Intermediary lay a short time in a small hotel

indicators.note: in places the wager and the brief spell within the small hotel

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel or pub with rooms
to lay money is to place a bet
Scots bide a wee means wait a short time, so a wee is a brief spell

explanation.surface: A go-between rested briefly at a little inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' looks like resting, but it is a wager, BET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in-between sits in the middle position, neither one thing nor the other.

clue.text: Warder who starts the game receiving pay rise

indicators.note: the beater is receiving, so taking inside, the pay word

parts.note: on a shoot a beater flushes out, or starts, the game birds

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the pay word reads upwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A referee who kicks off the match gets a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns FEE into EEF; 'starts the game' means flushing birds, not kicking off.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.

clue.text: Welsher fails in point-to-point — or in another place

indicators.note: in tells us the jumbled name sits inside the pair of points

parts.note: two compass points, each E for east

indicators.note: a welsher fails to pay, and the word fails signals the letters fall apart

explanation.surface: A bookmaker who won't pay up comes to grief at a country horse race, or somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase for hunting horses; a welsher is a bookie who won't pay. 'fails' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means somewhere other than here.

clue.text: Aquatic champion to make an appearance?

parts.note: surf is the breaking sea, an aquatic setting
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A top swimmer or surfer is set to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: SURF ACE reads as a champion of the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to come up to the top, to emerge into view.

clue.text: It presses double, by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals that the word for double is said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: a ringer is a lookalike or double

explanation.surface: Something that crushes things seems to come in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wringer is a mangle, a machine that squeezes water from laundry between rollers.

clue.text: Smollett goes around short of one shoe

indicators.note: short of means the reversed name lacks the letter for one
goes around means the forename is read backwards

parts.note: Tobias Smollett was an eighteenth-century Scottish novelist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The novelist Smollett wanders about with only one shoe on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes around' turns TOBIAS into SAIBOT; 'short of' removes the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog worn by peasants, especially in France.

clue.text: Singer with bribe managed nothing

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe
to run something is to manage it
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A vocalist who was offered a bribe accomplished nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest voice range.

clue.text: Bearer's no good in the bush

indicators.note: in places the letters for no good inside the bush

parts.note: a brier, or briar, is a thorny bush

explanation.surface: A porter is useless out in the wild scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bringer is one who carries or brings something, a carrier.

clue.text: He plays his part badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are poorly arranged, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor actor who fluffs his role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He plays' sounds theatrical; read whole, he is a player of a string instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp player plays a part in an orchestra; rearranged badly, the clue describes him.

clue.text: Force that's excessive, even though hurting only the leaders

indicators.note: only the leading letters of the five following words are taken

explanation.surface: A complaint that force is excessive, even when only the ringleaders are hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Legislation with teeth has real power to enforce, so the word means effective force.

clue.text: More vacuous politician joins the row

annotationWithheld.why: More vacuous politician joins the row (7): MP + TIER (row) gives MPTIER; nothing in the clue as printed (scan agrees) supplies the opening E
annotationWithheld.clue: More vacuous politician joins the row

clue.text: Argue with engineer about early retirement

indicators.note: the engineered word goes about, so surrounds, the early letter

parts.note: to engineer something craftily is to wangle it

indicators.note: early points to the first letter of retirement

explanation.surface: Someone quarrels with a technician over taking a pension ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' looks like a noun but is the verb, WANGLE; 'early' takes R from 'retirement'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to dispute noisily or at length.

clue.text: Group controlling Indian city backing a form of riot control

indicators.note: backing means the whole group-and-city run is read in reverse
the group controls, or holds within it, the Indian city

parts.note: a set is a group
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A gang running an Indian city supports one way of quelling disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlling' and 'backing' both act: the city sits in the group, and the whole run is turned round. Agra is home to the Taj Mahal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is a chemical agent sprayed by police to disperse crowds.

clue.text: Miss White takes shelter in surprise attack

parts.note: Pearl White was the star of silent film serials such as The Perils of Pauline
a harbour is a shelter

explanation.surface: A woman named White takes cover during an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearl White was an American silent-film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl Harbor was the Japanese surprise strike on the US Pacific fleet in December 1941.
